best_for: Developers who think better with a visual commit graph than with `git log`, and whose work is open source or local, or who will pay once private repos are in play.

points.title: Free stops at private repos
points.text: The free Community plan covers GitKraken Desktop, the CLI and GitLens, but only for local repos and public remotes. Opening a private remote on GitHub, GitLab or similar needs Pro or a higher plan.

points.title: Paid plans are sold by the seat
points.text: Pro covers up to 2 seats, Advanced up to 10 and Business up to 100, each billed per seat per month and paid yearly. Advanced adds self-hosted Git integrations and single-domain SSO. The pricing page did not show dollar amounts when we read it, so check it before you budget.

points.title: Proprietary, not open source
points.text: GitKraken is closed-source software. Git itself stays the same underneath, so your repositories keep working with the plain Git command line if you stop using it.

points.title: Recent systems only
points.text: The install guide lists Windows 10 or later and macOS 13 or later on Intel and Apple silicon. On Linux it names Ubuntu 18.04+, Debian 10+, RHEL 8+ and Fedora 39+, and says other distributions may work without official support.

points.title: Linux: the Flatpak is not the vendor's
points.text: GitKraken's own guide offers .deb, .rpm, .tar.gz and a Snap. The Flatpak listed here for x64 and Arm64 is an unverified Flathub wrapper, and Flathub notes it is not affiliated with or supported by Axosoft.

points.title: Windows installs per user
points.text: The Windows installer is 64-bit and installs for the current user, so no administrator rights are needed. Settings live in `AppData\Roaming\.gitkraken`.

points.title: Old versions mostly on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 25 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
